# CAIRN

> A command interface for coordinating rescue robots after an earthquake, where the map is
> incomplete, the radio is unreliable, and the robots keep discovering things that contradict
> each other. Built for the IEI BPDC UXcelerate! challenge, September 2026.

The reframe: a commander's job is not to drive robots, it is to decide what to believe and where
to spend time they do not have. The primary object of the interface is therefore a decision under
uncertainty, not a fleet.

## Design decisions

- Certainty is drawn as material — solid, stipple, hatch, void — never as colour alone, and it
  decays continuously with age, so ground nobody re-checks visibly fades.
- Contradictory observations raise a dispute rather than being silently resolved; both claims are
  attributed and the cost of each choice is shown in triage order.
- A robot that cannot be reached is never removed from the map; orders queue rather than fail.
- Every event carries two clocks — when it happened, and when Command learned it — so
  late-delivered observations arrive already stale and can revise the past.
